::: {#sol-batch-of-one}

A minibatch of one image has $\mu_j = z_{1j}$
and $\sigma_j^2 = 0$,
so every normalized [pre-activation](feedforward-networks.qmd#def-pre-activation) would be 0,
whatever the image.
The prediction would not depend on the image at all.

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
try:
    _ = batch_norm(pre[:1])
except ValueError as error:
    batch_of_one_error = str(error)
print(batch_of_one_error)
_ = batch_norm.eval()
one_image_output = batch_norm(pre[:1])
print(one_image_output.shape)
```

`nn.BatchNorm1d` treats a minibatch of one differently in its two modes:

- **Training mode.**
  It refuses the minibatch:
  "`r py$batch_of_one_error`".
- **Evaluation mode.**
  It uses its running averages instead,
  so it accepts a single image.

Evaluation mode is what makes predictions use the running averages.
That is why `train()` calls `net.eval()`
before it computes the test [accuracy](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-accuracy).

:::
